@ChrisBlueStone, I'm interested in trying your workaround, but I'm doubtful I'm commenting out the correct line. Can you confirm where you say "I noticed that if I comment out [this line](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/master/code/AssetLib/FBX/FBXConverter.cpp#L3264)", seems to be this:
`na->mNumScalingKeys = static_cast<unsigned int>(keyCount);`
@ChrisBlueStone, sorry never mind I see you specified the line `// mat.Decompose(s, r, t);`

Sorry about that. Linking to master probably wasn't the best idea. Here's the line on the branch at the time https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/411171fa459e521ff47974ac9ea7a32d222cecbd/code/AssetLib/FBX/FBXConverter.cpp#L3264

I think I could be experiencing this same issue. I am using an FBX model originally from Mixamo exported from Blender. I noticed in one of my animations the character's leg was 'snapping' to an incorrect transform for a split second. I thought it was something to do with the interpolation but after playing through the animation frame by frame I found it was the animation data itself. And seemingly the issue only occurs with rotations. I have tried ensuring that the W component within each quaternion is > 0.0 as suggested in this post: 'https://gamedev.stackexchange.com/questions/27547/frame-interpolation-issues-for-skeletal-animation'. But no luck. Here are what my animation frames look like:
First frame (before):
![Screenshot (260)](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/assets/50274957/e9a4e151-c210-46d3-829e-9c4f2b0a6261)
Second frame (incorrect / inverted rotation):
![Screenshot (261)](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/assets/50274957/4413626d-57fd-43d4-b870-f9d637d5c181)
Third frame (after)
![Screenshot (262)](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/assets/50274957/6bead969-252e-4e2f-a02e-b366a74f35a2)

I find it very bizarre that the rest of the animations load perfectly fine, while something has gone wrong with this single frame in this specific animation, leading me to believe it could be a bug with Assimp. I am wondering if anyone could confirm that the issue I am experiencing is the same as the issue listed in this post? If so, has it been fixed in recent versions of Assimp, or has anyone found a non-work-around fix? And if not, does anyone know what could be causing my issue?
I'm also experiencing this issue, any news on a possible fix or workaround?
@miguelibero, have you tried recompiling assimp with the above mentioned `mat.Decompose(s, r, t);` line commented out? That fixed it for me.

issue.body:
There are a number of FBX animation related issues open currently including: - `Bug introduced 27 Oct 2019:` #5808 - `Bug introduced 24 Mar 2020:` #3390 - #1974 - #4487 - #4550 - #4714 - #5131 - #5357 - #5449 ### Possible cause What seems to have happened is that bug #5808 was introduced on 27 Oct 2019, which went unreported for several months. Code continued to be added incrementally, and then bug #3390 was introduced on 24 Mar 2020; this bug also went unreported for many months and in the meantime a lot of complexity had been added to the FBX importer. Also, it's important to understand that bugs in the FBX code don't affect all FBX models. Some FBX models are affected by some bugs, while other FBX models are affected by other bugs; in the examples below, it can be observed that - "Nathan" model was unaffected by the first bug - "Sophia" and "Manuel" models were affected by both bugs* If a developer is only testing against a small set of models, it is unfortunately likely that new code may contain bugs which don't affect the local test FBX model(s), but which may affect other FBX models... *Manuel worked properly in release v5.3.1 while Nathan was broken (details table below), so I suspect v5.3.1 contained only the 2nd bug and not the first; for some reason "Manuel" showed artifacts due to 2nd bug on `master` branch but not in release 5.3.1 ### Bisect report: bug #5808 introduced on 27 Oct 2019 Details in issue 5808 [comment](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/issues/5808#issue-2580337271) ### Bisect report: bug #3390 introduced on 24 Mar 2020 Details in issue 3390 [comment](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/issues/3390#issuecomment-2408621190) ### (N - 1)st partial fix introduced in [`88a9598`](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/commit/88a9598ded4ab8a9a8742e5143a2eb406886655e) on 26 Apr 2022 At commit [`88a9598`](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/commit/88a9598ded4ab8a9a8742e5143a2eb406886655e) on 26 Apr 2022, "Manuel" got fixed and "Sophia" became less degraded (though was still "abstract art") ### Bisect report: Nth bug introduced in 28 Nov 2023 commit [`384db86`](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/commit/384db8686e84fe95afe417fd341fc259f528649d) "Manuel" broke again, Sophia got worse, and both "SilverDragon" and "TarislandDragon" completely broken Details in [below comment](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/issues/5719#issuecomment-2307928439) Anyone have any ideas on how to improve the situation? Another case where bugs got introduced several years ago and may be hard to address with all the additional code added during that period ### Observations To prevent these sorts of things happening in future, would be useful to have a minimal set of carefully selected test FBX models in the repo with guidelines that their animation must not be broken by any code updates (i.e. the set of models would need to be manually tested before committing modifications) #### Difficulties correlating assimp releases with repo main branch Due to the highly selective cherry-picking when creating assimp releases, it is often not possible to compare a release against a commit to the repo main branch even if they are around the same point in time. An example is the table in [issue 5449](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/issues/5449#issuecomment-2023986936) where it can be seen that the "Manuel" model was still working at release 5.3.1 from 2023, despite having been broken on the main repo branch since 2019; and "Nathan," which was broken at the 24 Mar 2020 commit, was also broken in 5.3.1 -- as mentioned above, my theory (which of course may well be wrong) is that v5.3.1 only had the second bug, not the first, which would have broken all three models ("Sophia", "Nathan" and "Manuel") so it's a mystery why only "Manuel" was not broken in release 5.3.1
